summary: The USA 6G Global Leadership Act requires the Ambassador at Large for Cyberspace and Digital Policy to coordinate U.S. diplomatic efforts ahead of major international telecommunication conferences. It directs federal agencies to promote trusted telecommunications vendors, counter foreign influence in standards bodies, report on international actions by China and Russia, and prioritize development projects using U.S. or allied technology.

affected_groups.effect: Must coordinate diplomatic efforts, promote candidates for ITU leadership, conduct briefings, and produce required reports for Congress.
affected_groups.group: Federal Agencies (State Department, Department of Commerce, etc.)

affected_groups.effect: Consulted by the State Department regarding perspectives on the ITU elections process and engagement in standard-setting bodies.
May receive priority project assistance, connectivity support, and development loans or investments using trusted vendors and U.S. or allied technology.

key_provisions: Designates the Ambassador at Large for Cyberspace and Digital Policy to coordinate U.S. diplomatic efforts for the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference and the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference.
Requires the Ambassador to promote candidates for ITU leadership bodies, consult with private sector entities, and provide quarterly briefings to Congress.
Requires the Secretary of State to submit a report within 90 days detailing actions by China and Russia to influence the ITU and constrain digital freedom.

Directs the Secretary of State, International Development Finance Corporation, and Trade and Development Agency to carry out projects promoting trusted telecommunications infrastructure and prioritizing U.S. and allied technology.
Requires a report detailing the U.S. strategy to promote and dominate 6G technology globally within 90 days of enactment.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations authorized to carry out the projects and reporting requirements.
Explicit definitions for terms like 'trusted vendors' beyond general references to U.S. companies and allies.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The USA 6G Global Leadership Act requires the Ambassador at Large for Cyberspace and Digital Policy to coordinate U.S. diplomatic efforts ahead of major international telecommunication conferences. It directs federal agencies to promote trusted telecommunications vendors, counter foreign influence in standards bodies, report on international actions by China and Russia, and prioritize development projects using U.S. or allied technology.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation directs federal diplomatic and development resources toward international standard-setting bodies and telecommunications infrastructure, aiming to secure U.S. technological leadership in 6G and emerging technologies against foreign influence.
